text: I'm going to hurt a lot of men's feelings with this one. But the reason why a lot of your parents and grandparents stayed together for so long isn't necessarily because the relationship was healthy. It's because the women in those generations were financially trapped. You see, a woman back then couldn't just pick up her bags and leave. She relied on a man for survival. So, she stayed and she endured, even if she felt unsafe or unloved. But today, a woman can pay her own bills and build her own life. And with that kind of freedom, a man's value isn't in what he provides financially, it's in the quality of the man he actually is, how he treats her, how he speaks to her, and how safe, respected, and emotionally secure she feels beside him. And that right there is why there's a male loneliness epidemic. This message is not completely wrong, but it's not completely right either. Is it true that in the past, women were more financially dependent on men? Sure. And you can even go further. Social pressure was stronger, religion mattered more, divorce laws were stricter, and people were expected to endure even unhappy relationships. So yes, women living was harder. But here's the problem. One true statement doesn't automatically explain another. Even if women were more financially dependent back then, that alone does not explain the so-called male loneliness epidemic today. It might influence it a little, but it's not the main explanation. Because what changed is not only women's freedom, what changed is the entire dating marketplace. In my opinion, one of the biggest drivers here is technology, which changed dating through supply and demand. To show the shortcomings of his logic, I'd use an analogy. In the past, people also stayed at the same job much longer. Working decades in the same company was normal. Today, people change jobs much more often. Is it because people became less dependent on salaries from their jobs? Of course not. People depend on that money just as much as before, if not more. So finances alone do not fully explain why job loyalty changed. A major reason is that today there are simply more opportunities, and it is much easier to access them. You can go on LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, and apply to hundreds of jobs in a day. Technology created a far larger and more visible supply of options. And dating works the same way now. Social media and dating apps created a seemingly unlimited supply of potential partners. Now, someone will ask, but doesn't that mean men also have unlimited options? In theory, yes. In reality, not exactly. Because the demand works differently. Women are generally pickier than men, and hypergamy plays a role. Meaning women tend to prefer men who are taller, higher status, and earn more. So when women suddenly have unlimited access to men, the result is that the majority of women compete for a minority of men. That is where you hear things like 80% of women go for 20% of men. So ironically, even though women are less financially dependent today, many still want a man who is more successful than them in multiple areas, including financially. And when technology amplifies choice, this creates a system where average men struggle more than ever. So no, it's not as simple as women used to be trapped, now they are free. That's one piece of the puzzle. But the deeper reasons are supply, demand, and the way technology changed dating completely.
